title: Silca launches range of wide tubeless tyres for gravel and road use
content:
Cyclist
Silca launches range of wide tubeless tyres for gravel and road use

Silca has launched its own range of performance tyres for road and gravel racing. Called the Protocol, the new tyres come in 29mm, 34mm and 38mm widths for road use and 45mm, 50mm and 55mm for gravel. There’s also a 32-inch gravel tyre.

According to Silca CEO Josh Poertner, ‘For years, the industry approached gravel tyres by just slapping thick, heavy rubber onto traditional road tyre carcasses. We approached the Protocol lineup by first looking at lower-pressure dynamics. 

‘By optimising casing ply angles, tread profiles, and material science together, we’ve created a tyre platform that is faster, lighter, and more supple without sacrificing durability.’

The on-trend widths are accompanied by tech that comes from XC MTB tyres, which Silca says makes its new tyres faster and more durable than competitor products, despite 120TPI casings that are claimed to be thinner. It says that the thinner, higher-density casing helps the tyres to deflect impact forces, reducing flats and increasing compliance, while offering lower weight and rolling resistance.

Silca says that in developing the Protocol tyres it has had to balance a wide range of factors from rolling efficiency and grip to aerodynamics and rim compatibility, with a different mix of performance characteristics for each tyre’s expected use. 

All the tyres share the same silica rubber compound, which Silca calls Pulsar, and the same Race casing. There’s a carbon bead, in place of the more usual Kevlar, and a lightweight puncture protection layer that it calls Ghost, and that it claims is designed for rolling efficiency. There’s a second puncture protection layer, named SealSkin, which replaces Ghost and is built into some tyres for enhanced puncture protection.  

Silca’s rubber-related products range has progressively expanded, with the brand offering everything from tubeless sealant, rim tape and valves to TPU tubes and an online pressure calculation tool and it says the new tyres were designed to work with its existing product range. It sells you the necessary array of mini-pumps, track pumps and electric inflators too.

All the tyres are tubeless-ready and Silca provides a list of recommended minimum volumes of its sealant to use with each tyre and tyre width. It has signed up to sponsor gravel pro Dylan Johnson to race with the tyres.

Three gravel tread patterns

Gravel tyres need to match the surface conditions, so Silca offers three different tread patterns, all in 45mm, 50mm and 55mm widths.

Protocol RCG-1 tyres have a lower profile directional tread and Ghost puncture protection for fast gravel riding, mixed with on-tarmac use. Silca claims the following weights:

  • 45mm: 460g
  • 50mm: 510g
  • 55mm: 535g

Protocol RCG-3 tyres are designed for mixed surfaces and exchange the Ghost for SealSkin puncture protection. There’s a 32-inch tyre in 2.4-inch width, in addition to the three 700c tyres. Claimed tyre weights are:

  • 45mm: 495g
  • 50mm: 540g
  • 55mm: 590g
  • 32×2.4in: 710g

Finally, the Protocol RCG-4 tyre is designed for rough, loose technical terrain and mud and again uses the SealSkin puncture protection layer. Claimed weights are:

  • 45mm: 545g
  • 50mm: 620g
  • 55mm: 650g

Protocol road tyre range

Silca says that the road tyre range is also adapted for all-road riding and spans the modern tyre widths-as-measured for 25mm width rims, up to the largest width that most modern road bike frames can fit. It has a directional tread pattern that is claimed to be aerodynamically efficient. 

There’s just one tread pattern, Protocol RCR, which Silca says has the following weights:

  • 29mm: 290g
  • 34mm: 320g
  • 38mm: 350g

Protocol tyre prices

All the Protocol tyres for both road and gravel are priced at £99 / $99 / €119 / AU$159.95. The tyres will be available to purchase from Silca retailers and directly from Silca.
